sources.quote: The GOP-aligned groups (America PAC, Donald J. Trump For President 2024, Inc., Duty To America, Make America Great Again Inc., Right For America And Securing American Greatness Inc) spent about $700-$850k targeting young men last week
sources.searcher_note: Google/YouTube ad-library analysis naming Securing American Greatness Inc among GOP groups gender- and age-targeting young men in October 2024. No share-of-spend figure for SAG. Original URL youngmenresearchinitiative.substack.com redirects here.

sources.outlet: Brennan Center for Justice, Anna Massoglia
sources.quote: About 320 groups that do not disclose their donors collectively spent more than $281 million on online ads during the 2024 election cycle without disclosing any spending to the FEC.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: online ads by groups with no FEC disclosure. Separately names SAG: 'Securing American Greatness, after its incorporation in March 2024, spent more than $81 million, about $67 million of which went to super PACs.' No EIN-only Google total.

sources.outlet: The New York Times (syndicated on GV Wire), Shane Goldmacher and Theodore Schleifer
sources.quote: The group has spent at least $44 million since early last year, sending nearly $25 million to super PACs and airing about $19 million of ads boosting Trump and Republicans.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff coverage naming SAG as Trump's dark-money nonprofit in the 2026 midterms. Nothing on Google, EIN verification or gender targeting.

sources.outlet: Brennan Center / OpenSecrets / Wesleyan Media Project
sources.quote: Of the $619 million in spending in our sample, 45 percent came from spenders that may conceal some or all of their donors.
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: Google plus Meta political spending by donor-concealing spenders in 2024. Does not split out EIN-only vs FEC-ID Google buyers; does not name SAG.

sources.quote: Advertisers wishing to apply for verification before this date may do so using our existing political verification form and a FEC ID or EIN.
sources.searcher_note: Supports the lead's caveat: in November 2019 Google widened election ads to state-level candidates and ballot measures, so EIN or state-registration verification is a normal, legal route for non-federal buyers.

sources.quote: Securing American Greatness spent $81 million in the election, including $67 million in contributions to Trump-supporting super PACs.
sources.searcher_note: Names SAG as a pro-Trump nonprofit that does not disclose donors, with 2024 totals. Nothing on Google or gender targeting.

notes: No source reports the aggregate finding: 8,368 EIN-only US Google buyers spending $861.4M vs $1,389.1M for FEC-ID buyers. No source gives SAG's one-gender share (84%) of its 2024 Google spend. The closest match is the Young Men Research Project post (Oct 2024), which names SAG among GOP groups targeting young men on Google/YouTube. Also seen but not recorded because X pages cannot be verified: an Andrew Arenge X post (x.com/MrArenge/status/1800335677151949191) saying SAG began Google-targeting an ad at Pennsylvania towns on June 6, 2024, $80K for 5M+ impressions. InfluenceWatch (page dated 2026-05-29) says SAG spent $55M on issue advocacy advertising and $25M on direct mail in 2024. The Hill's 2026 midterm-ad piece returned 403.
